---
title: Home
---

This example demonstrates **incremental rebuilds**. Quarto 2 has
two render modes:

- **Mode A — full project render.** Triggered by
  `quarto render <project-dir>` (or just `quarto render` with no
  args from inside the project). Re-runs Pass 2 (the body render)
  for every page. Pass 1 (the static profile) hits a content-hash
  keyed cache, so unchanged inputs aren't re-extracted.
- **Mode B — subset render.** Triggered by naming specific files:
  `quarto render posts/first.qmd`. Only the named files re-run
  Pass 2. The sidebar / navbar / cross-doc indices are still
  consistent because Pass 1 still runs over every project file
  (warm from cache for unchanged inputs).

Pass 2 is **never** cached. The reason: Pass 2 runs user-supplied
Lua filters and language engines, which can have side effects
(network calls, time, randomness). Caching the bytes they produce
would silently break reproducibility for any non-pure filter. The
narrower `freeze` feature (separate epic, opt-in per chunk) caches
engine output explicitly when the user knows it's safe.

The win from Mode B isn't "Pass 2 was cached" — it's "Pass 2 didn't
need to run for unaffected pages."

See [About](about.qmd) and the [first post](posts/first.qmd).
